key_facts: Microsoft has terminated its involvement in Nscale's planned AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, which was announced as the UK's largest AI data centre with a £2bn pledge; the BBC reports this based on its understanding, and Microsoft declined to comment.

Nscale says it remains committed to the Loughton project and is exploring alternative power sources for the site; its relationship with Microsoft remains strong for other projects in Norway, Portugal and the United States.
The Telegraph reported that Nscale was told the site's power supply, originally due at the end of the year, will not arrive until the 2030s, due to a London-wide grid issue.

The Loughton site was expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens; in the previous month Microsoft had announced that part of its $30bn (£22bn) UK investment would fund the Loughton supercomputer.
importance_reason: Заметный сбой в крупном инфраструктурном AI-проекте в Великобритании с задержкой энергоснабжения до 2030-х, но без прямого влияния на макро- или рыночные показатели.
market_link: Возможное влияние на инвестиционные планы Microsoft и Nscale в Великобритании и на спрос на энергетическую инфраструктуру Лондона; прямой эффект на котировки неочевиден.

key_facts: Home sellers in Britain cut asking prices on more than 3,000 properties a day on average in September, according to Rightmove figures shared exclusively with the BBC; the total was the highest of any month for 15 years.

The average price reduction was nearly 7%, equivalent to nearly £21,000 cut from a typically valued home. Homes with a price reduction took 119 days to find a buyer, versus 39 days for those listed at one price.

34% of listed homes had a price reduction in September, slightly below the recent peak of 36% in September 2023. Zoopla reported listings up 5% year on year while agreed sales fell 9%, with mortgage rates at a three-year high.
importance_reason: Notable housing-market signal with mortgage rates at three-year highs, but a sectoral data story without a direct central bank or policy trigger.
market_link: Rising mortgage rates and weaker housing demand may weigh on UK housing-related equities, mortgage lenders and bank mortgage books, and on UK inflation and rate expectations via housing activity.

key_facts: Criminals are using AI to make scams more convincing, including fake retailer websites that claim to be family-owned UK firms but often deliver nothing or cheap mass-produced goods, according to trading standards officers.

National Trading Standards has published an AI scam watchlist covering AI-generated images, voice cloning and deepfake videos used to extract money from people, including impersonation of family members or friends asking for money in an 'emergency' and AI-driven romance scams sustained over weeks or months.
Consumer group Which? says typos and grammatical errors can no longer be relied on to identify scams, because AI can generate error-free personalised phishing messages at scale.

Recommended protection includes never sending money, gift cards or personal/financial information to someone not met in person, checking shop addresses and FCA Firm Checker, verifying job adverts directly with the business, and treating pressure or urgency as a warning sign. Fraud can be reported to Report Fraud or the Citizens Advice Consumer Helpline (0808 223 1133).
importance_reason: Consumer-protection advisory without market impact; relevant to personal finance but no direct effect on markets or macro indicators.

key_facts: Yuriy Ryzhenkov, CEO of Metinvest, called on the EU to drop or carve out Ukraine from recently imposed steel import restrictions, calling them 'unfair' and imposed 'without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in'.

The EU capped steel imports tax-free at 18.3 million tonnes per year, a 47% reduction from 2024 levels; Ukraine has a country-specific quota that the EU says guarantees exports but at a 'level lower than in the past years'. The Ukrainian steel industry estimates EU steel exports could fall by about 50-60%.

The EU is Ukraine's top steel customer; before the 2022 full-scale invasion metallurgy and mining accounted for roughly 10% of national income and a third of exports. Ryzhenkov said strikes on steel mills 'intensified significantly recently' and that in September Ukraine produced 'no single tonne of steel' for the first time in about 150 years.
importance_reason: Значимое торговое решение ЕС с прямым эффектом на ключевой экспортный сектор Украины, но в рамках региональных торговых мер без системного макроэффекта.
market_link: Сокращение квоты на импорт стали в ЕС может давить на европейские и украинские цены на сталь и на финансовые результаты металлургов; эффект на широкие рынки ограничен.

key_facts: Passengers who play loud music on buses in England could be fined up to £100 under a government attempt to crack down on antisocial behaviour, which also targets littering, vaping and threatening behaviour on public transport.

New guidance was issued to local authorities on powers introduced earlier this year; they still need sign-off from the Transport Secretary. Authorised officers, including Transport Safety Officers and the Police, will enforce the rules, not bus drivers.

A national campaign, "share the carriage, not the noise", is being launched for rail passengers. Under existing powers, passengers who refuse to stop can be removed from a train or fined up to £1,000.

Opposition and union figures welcomed the measures as a step but said enforcement is the key issue: Richard Holden MP cited a 68% rise in assaults against rail staff, and Olly Glover MP said the rules are meaningless without funded transport safety officers on the ground.
importance_reason: Domestic transport-policy measure with limited direct market impact; no effect on macro, energy or financial variables.

key_facts: China's GDP grew by 4.5% in the third quarter, up from 4.3% in the previous period but below the 5% expansion recorded from January to March, according to official Chinese data.
The 4.5% figure is at the bottom end of Beijing's annual growth target of 4.5%-5%.

Exports rose on AI-related demand for computer chips and data-centre components, offsetting weak domestic spending; property investment fell by more than 20% in the first nine months from the same period last year.

China's trade surplus is on track to overtake the record $1.2tn seen last year; in September Beijing unveiled support measures including lower interest rates for some businesses and subsidies for property buyers.

key_facts: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund that will make donations for the "public good"; the fund could receive another 2% of shares at its board's discretion.
The announcement comes as Anthropic prepares a potential stock market listing (IPO) that could value the firm at more than $1tn (£750bn).

Anthropic told prospective investors that its revenue rose 45% to $16.8bn (£12.6bn) in the three months to the end of September. The Public Benefit Fund's shares would not be used for lobbying or political donations in the US or overseas.
Research by the IMF published in 2024 suggested that almost 40% of jobs around the world will be affected by AI, rising to as high as 60% in advanced economies.
